slides.heading: if Statements
slides.body: if Statements is part of Conditional Execution. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: if Statements
slides.body: An if statement runs an indented block only when its condition is True. If the condition is False, the block is skipped.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: An if statement is like a gate that opens only when the correct ticket is shown.

annotations.note: This line stores or updates a value using a variable.
This line checks a condition before running the indented code.
This line displays a value or message on the screen.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: A conditional needs a colon, correct indentation, and a condition that clearly evaluates to True or False.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Print Bring umbrella only when is_raining is True.
slides.hint: Write if is_raining: then indent the print line.

quiz.prompt_text: What happens to an if block when its condition is False?

options: It runs the block with a warning message
It skips the indented block entirely
It asks the user to correct the condition

quiz.explanation: When the condition is False, Python skips the entire indented block and continues with the rest of the program.

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines to print Hot day only when temperature exceeds 28.
quiz.explanation: The variable is assigned first, then the if checks the condition, and the indented print executes only when temperature > 28 is True.

quiz.prompt_text: Write an if statement that prints Bring umbrella only when is_raining is True.

content.hint: Write if is_raining: then indent the print line on the next line.

quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: if is_raining: with indented print below it. Python only runs the indented code when the condition evaluates to True.
